key_insight: High-throughput first-principles screening shows delafossite and related ordered rock-salt layered oxides can compete with infinite-layer ABO2 phases in stability, especially for nickelates and even more for palladate/platinate analogs.
engineering_relevance: These stability trends help narrow synthesis targets for bulk substrate-free infinite-layer oxides and guide cation/doping choices for designing new correlated-electron and superconducting materials.
method: Comprehensive high-throughput first-principles simulations across AB O2 compositions
Phase-diagram comparison of four layered oxide motifs: infinite-layer, delafossite, and ordered rock-salt (111) variants
Electronic-structure analysis of Fermi-surface character and cation ordering
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a computed stability phase diagram and electronic-structure comparisons showing delafossites rival infinite-layer phases in thermodynamic stability for nickelates, with even stronger competition in palladates and platinates.
watch_item: Bulk thermodynamic stability does not guarantee easy experimental realization; epitaxial strain, oxygen control, and synthesis kinetics may still favor different phases.
paper_title: Delafossites as an unexpected competing phase to infinite-layer oxides
